title: Moroni writes to Pahoran
summary: Moroni writes an epistle to Pahoran, chief judge and governor, and to those chosen to govern the affairs of the war.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni writes again to Pahoran, governor of the land, in the city of Zarahemla, and addresses those chosen to govern and manage the war.

unspecified_visual_details: The place where Moroni writes, writing materials, clothing, and appearance.

narration.text: Behold, I direct mine epistle to Pahoran

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Pahoran or other addressees as present; this verse presents them as recipients of the letter.

title: An accusation of neglect
summary: An unnamed speaker condemns the addressees, recalls their appointment to gather and arm men, reports suffering among his men and Helaman’s men, reports thousands fallen by the sword, and asks the cause of the neglect.

explicit_facts.text: The addressees were appointed to gather and arm men and send them against Lamanites entering their land.
The speaker says that he and his men, and Helaman and his men, have suffered hunger, thirst, fatigue, and other afflictions.
The speaker says they would not complain if those sufferings were all they had endured.
The speaker reports that thousands of their people have fallen by the sword and says the addressees neglected to provide sufficient strength and aid.
The speaker asks the cause of the neglect.

unspecified_visual_details: Whether this address is spoken or written.

narration.text: I have somewhat to say unto them by the way of condemnation
myself, and also my men, and also Helaman and his men, have suffered exceedingly great sufferings
great has been the slaughter among our people
we desire to know the cause of this exceedingly great neglect

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The suffering and deaths are reported, not narrated as events occurring during this address.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the unnamed speaker or addressees by name.
Do not depict a present battle, injury, or death.
Do not assume the address is a letter or a face-to-face speech.

title: A charge against idle leaders
summary: Moroni charges the leaders with sitting idle while their people need protection, armies, and provisions, and says many have perished hungry while serving the people's welfare.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni accuses the leaders of sitting on their thrones while enemies kill thousands of their brethren.
Moroni says the leaders could have sent armies to strengthen and save people who looked to them for protection.
Moroni says provisions were withheld and many fought while near death from hunger.
Moroni says the leaders neglected their brethren and that God knew the cries and sufferings of those slain.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The accusation may be conveyed as Moroni's written voice over an otherwise unspecified setting.
unspecified_visual_details: Whether any imagined addressees or battle imagery appear; their appearance and the writing location.

narration.text: Can you think to sit upon your thrones
ye have withheld your provisions from them

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The reported deaths and suffering are not narrated as a present visual event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the leaders physically on thrones as a literal event; the verse uses this as an accusation.

title: The slain enter the Lord's rest
summary: Moroni rejects the idea that those killed were wicked or lost, saying the Lord allows the righteous to be slain and that they enter God's rest. He fears judgment because of governmental sloth and neglect.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni says the righteous may be slain so God's justice and judgment may come upon the wicked, and that they enter the rest of the Lord their God.
Moroni fears God's judgments will come upon the people because of the government's sloth and neglect.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The teaching can be presented as off-screen narration over a neutral setting.
unspecified_visual_details: Any visible depiction of God, the Lord's rest, or the slain; setting and appearance.

narration.text: they do enter into the rest of the Lord their God
I fear exceedingly that the judgments of God will come upon this people

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord's rest is a teaching, not a described visible place or event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a heavenly setting or divine figure; no appearance or visual description is supplied.

title: The cost of internal division
summary: Moroni argues that internal wickedness and conflict by the king-men weakened the people. He reports that Lamanites are now taking lands, killing people, and carrying women and children away captive.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni says internal wickedness and the war among the people enabled their enemies to gain power.
Moroni says the king-men fought against their own people instead of joining them against their enemies.
Moroni reports that Lamanites are taking lands, killing people, and carrying women and children captive.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The letter can carry the report of these events without depicting them as occurring now.
unspecified_visual_details: The place where Moroni writes and the appearance of the referenced groups or captives.

narration.text: the Lamanites are coming upon us
this because of the great wickedness of those who are seeking for power and authority

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lamanite attacks and captivity are reported events, not a present-tense scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an attack, killing, or captivity happening in this scene.

title: Questions about loyalty and aid
summary: Moroni questions whether the leaders seek power or have become traitors, and asks whether they have forgotten past deliverances and are idle while people at the borders fall by the sword.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni questions whether the addressees seek authority or are traitors.
Moroni asks whether they have withheld food and men because they are secure in the country's heart.
Moroni asks whether they have forgotten the Lord's commandments, their fathers' captivity, and past deliverances.
Moroni describes people sitting idle while people at the borders are falling by the sword, wounded and bleeding.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The questions may be rendered as Moroni's off-screen letter over an unspecified setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The exact location and appearance of any persons referenced in Moroni's questions.

narration.text: Have ye forgotten the commandments of the Lord your God?
while there are thousands round about in the borders of the land who are falling by the sword

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The border violence is described in a rhetorical question and should not be converted into a separate present-tense battle scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict past captivity or deliverances; they are referenced, not narrated here as current events.

title: Cleanse the inward vessel
summary: Moroni says God will not regard the leaders as guiltless if they remain idle, invokes the teaching that the inward vessel must be cleansed first, and demands repentance and aid for the armies.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni says God will not regard the leaders as guiltless if they sit still and behold these things.
Moroni cites the teaching that the inward vessel shall be cleansed first, then the outer vessel.
Moroni calls on the addressees to repent, act, and send food and men to him and Helaman.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The teaching and demand are delivered as the voice of the letter over a neutral setting.
unspecified_visual_details: Any literal vessel, its appearance, and the place where Moroni writes.

narration.text: the inward vessel shall be cleansed first
begin to be up and doing

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The inward and outer vessels are figurative teaching, not literal objects or a cleansing event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict literal vessels being cleaned or a supernatural judgment.

title: Moroni's warning of action
summary: Moroni says he will leave some freemen to maintain the land if the leaders do not aid the armies. He says he will come to those who desire freedom and oppose those seeking power, and declares that he takes up his sword to defend his country.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni says he will leave some freemen to maintain the land if the letter is not granted and aid is not provided.
Moroni attributes the freemen's capacity to their faith and patience in tribulation.
Moroni says he will come to those who desire freedom and stir up insurrections against those who seek power.
Moroni says he takes his sword according to God's commandments to defend his country.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni may be shown with a sword as the letter refers to his taking it up.
unspecified_visual_details: Moroni's appearance, the sword's design, and the location.

narration.text: I do take my sword to defend the cause of my country

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The threatened future insurrection is not an event occurring in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an insurrection or battle as already underway.

title: A demand for assistance
summary: Moroni warns the leaders to defend their country and children, demands assistance, and threatens to come to Zarahemla and use force if they impede the people's freedom. He contrasts the causes of Lamanite and governmental wrongdoing.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni warns that the leaders must defend their country and children or face the sword of justice.
Moroni says he is waiting for assistance and will come to Zarahemla and strike if they do not relieve the armies.
Moroni says the Lord will not allow the leaders to prosper in iniquity and destroy the righteous people.
Moroni contrasts Lamanite hatred rooted in inherited tradition and dissent with the leaders' love of glory and worldly things.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The warnings are best conveyed as the letter's voice; no threatened action is shown as occurring.
unspecified_visual_details: Moroni's location while composing the letter and any visual representation of justice or divine judgment.

narration.text: Behold, I wait for assistance from you
I come unto you, even in the land of Zarahemla

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The sword of justice is figurative; the threatened journey and strike are future conditional actions.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a divine sword, divine appearance, or Moroni arriving in Zarahemla.

title: Moroni closes his epistle
summary: Moroni says the governors must repent or face battle, urges the leaders to send provisions and men to him and Helaman, and warns that he will come if they refuse. He closes by stating that he seeks God's glory and his country's freedom and welfare.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni reports the Lord's warning that the people will go to battle against appointed governors if they do not repent.
Moroni asks the addressees to send provisions and men to him and Helaman.
Moroni says he will come speedily and obtain food even by the sword if necessary.
Moroni identifies himself as chief captain, says he seeks not power or worldly honor, and closes his epistle.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni may be shown finishing the letter; the exact setting is not stated.
unspecified_visual_details: Writing materials, Moroni's appearance, and the place where he writes.

narration.text: And thus I close mine epistle.
I seek not for power, but to pull it down.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord's quoted message is reported by Moroni, not a separately narrated visible appearance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Moroni's threatened journey, battle, or taking of food by force as occurring now.
